papers.title: TRAF7 mutations stabilize K/NRAS and hyperactivate MAPK signaling to cause CAFDADD neurodevelopmental defects.
papers.summary: TRAF7 normally promotes K/NRAS polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, restraining MAPK signaling. CAFDADD-associated TRAF7 variants act dominantly, causing KRAS/NRAS accumulation and constitutive ERK1/2 hyperactivation, with premature cortical neurogenesis defects in patient iPSC-derived organoids and knock-in mice. The MEK inhibitor selumetinib partially rescued these phenotypes, identifying impaired RAS ubiquitination as a targetable disease mechanism.

papers.title: Converting lysosomes into photothermal organelles enables nanoparticle-free tumor ablation via intracellular vapor bubbles.
papers.summary: The authors exploit lysosomal pH trapping of cationic amphiphilic dyes to convert lysosomes into endogenous photothermal reactors. Pulsed laser activation of dye-enriched lysosomes forms intracellular vapor bubbles that ablate cancer cells in 2D cultures, 3D spheroids, patient-derived neuroblastoma tumoroids, and ovarian tumor fragments - achieving nanoparticle-free, low-fluence photothermal therapy using sunitinib and a commercial dye.

papers.title: A designed ubiquitin-binding protein selectively enriches and visualizes unanchored ubiquitin.
papers.summary: Using affinity maturation and RFdiffusion-based computational design, the authors engineered proteins that specifically bind unanchored ubiquitin. The optimized ubip10 enriched unanchored ubiquitin from cells and influenza A virions, quantified its cellular levels, and imaging revealed a previously unknown unanchored ubiquitin coat surrounding aggresomes, providing a selective tool for studying this poorly understood ubiquitin pool.

papers.title: Deep learning extracts MoA-specific signatures from high-throughput images of chemically and genetically perturbed Corynebacteria.
papers.summary: A deep learning model classifies antibiotic mechanisms of action directly from high-throughput microscopy images of drug-treated Corynebacterium glutamicum, a tuberculosis surrogate. It recognizes previously unseen modes of action, links chemical and genetic perturbation images for target prediction, and recovered known cell-cycle biology, enabling MoA-aware phenotypic screening for anti-TB drug discovery.

papers.title: Population coding under the scale invariance of high-dimensional noise.
papers.summary: In mouse V1, stimulus information in high-dimensional population activity scales with neuron number without saturating. Scale-invariant noise components are not aligned with the signal enough to bound information, which depends on the full noise eigenspectrum rather than leading modes. Under subsampling, any information-limiting correlations must be differential correlations, clarified via power-law analyses.

papers.title: Multimodal profiling of atherosclerosis: Protocol and pilot data for the AtherOMICS biobank.
papers.summary: The AtherOMICS biobank links multiomic plaque phenotyping with blood banking, in vivo imaging, and clinical data; 246 endarterectomy patients are enrolled. Single-nucleus RNA-seq (n=17) confirmed macrophages as the dominant plaque cell type, paired plaque-plasma proteomics (n=88) quantified 2,841 shared proteins with low plaque-plasma correlation, and cross-modality image integration was feasible.

papers.title: Specific and efficient translation inhibition-transcription activation resistance module against viruses in plants.
papers.summary: The authors built a virus-activated synthetic immune circuit in which viral subgenomic RNA production triggers a translation-inhibition-transcription-activation module expressing resistance-inducing proteins. The circuit conferred resistance against PepMV, TMV, and CMV in Nicotiana benthamiana, tomato, and Arabidopsis, with cross-resistance and no growth penalty, offering a programmable antiviral platform for crops.

papers.title: mTORC1-TFEB/TFE3 signaling is associated with bile acid diversification during hepatic metabolic adaptation.
papers.summary: Altered hepatic mTORC1-TFEB/TFE3 signaling is associated with remodeling of bile acid metabolism: depending on mTORC1 state, changes in Cyp2c70 and Cyp8b1 expression and cholesterol trafficking shift bile acids between non-12-OH and 12-OH species. Protein restriction reshaped bile acid profiles in mice and correlated with improved metabolic outcomes in MASLD patients.

papers.title: Distinct Arp2/3 isocomplexes drive axonal actin ring assembly and integrity.
papers.summary: Superresolution imaging places Arp2/3, the branched actin nucleator, within the axonal membrane periodic skeleton. Isoform-specific perturbation shows distinct isocomplexes act sequentially: Arpc1a/Arpc5-containing complexes assemble actin rings during early skeleton formation, while Arpc1b/Arpc5L complexes maintain rings in mature axons, revealing a developmental switch in isocomplex composition governing the axonal actin nanoarchitecture.

papers.title: Macrophage restriction in Drosophila wounds and tumors via a matrix degradation-moderating protease inhibitor.
papers.summary: Drosophila TEP3, ortholog of human CD109, limits macrophage attachment to wounded and transformed epithelia by inhibiting MMP1, reducing production of a basement-membrane damage signal. Tumors upregulate TEP3 to evade macrophage-dependent immune restriction, accelerating progression - showing fly cancers exploit a physiological anti-inflammatory axis to escape immune surveillance.

papers.title: CCR5 blockade inhibits menstrual-driven proinflammatory T cell infiltration into the cervicovaginal mucosa of women.
papers.summary: Tracking CD4 T cells across the menstrual cycle in women, plus a murine menstruation model, shows endometrial remodeling recruits bystander-activated CD4 T cells into cervicovaginal tissue in a CCR5-dependent manner. The CCR5 antagonist maraviroc substantially reduced this infiltration, suggesting an immunomodulatory approach for menstrual cycle-driven inflammatory conditions of the female reproductive tract.

papers.title: Cell-intrinsic functions of PD-L1 activate autophagy and prevent cytokine-induced apoptosis.
papers.summary: Thyroidal PD-L1 acts cell-intrinsically as a cytoprotective regulator: suppressing it in thyrocytes aberrantly activates AKT-ERK-mTORC1, inhibits autophagy, and promotes cytokine-induced apoptosis. In a mouse immune-checkpoint-inhibitor thyroiditis model, anti-PD-L1 triggered immune attack while promoting thyrocyte apoptosis, indicating ICI thyroid toxicity reflects both immune activation and intrinsic cellular vulnerability.

papers.title: Mechanism of GPR84 allosteric modulation at a helix 8-proximate site.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM structures of GPR84-Gi complexes identify a helix 8-proximate allosteric site for the positive allosteric modulator PSB-16671, connected to the orthosteric site by a polar residue network. The modulator stabilizes a Gi-biased conformation disfavoring beta-arrestin, sustaining macrophage phagocytosis of cancer cells without desensitization, establishing design principles for biased GPCR allostery.

papers.title: Engineering plant tandem kinase immune receptors expands effector recognition profiles.
papers.summary: The barley and wheat tandem kinase proteins RMO2 and RWT7 recognize different blast fungus effectors through their integrated HMA domains using distinct protein interfaces with nanomolar affinity. Structural analysis identified interface residues governing recognition and enabled engineering of dual-specificity receptors, establishing HMA domains as programmable modules for designing crop immune receptor specificities.

papers.title: Thalamofrontal synaptic weakening underlies short-term memory deficits from adolescent NMDAR hypofunction.
papers.summary: Repeated adolescent NMDA receptor antagonism (ketamine) in mice impairs short-term memory by reducing presynaptic release probability and short-term depression at mediodorsal thalamus-to-dmPFC synapses, with diminished direction-selective population coding. Chemogenetic strengthening of these projections restored neural selectivity and behavior, identifying a projection-specific presynaptic mechanism and therapeutic target for schizophrenia-related thalamofrontal dysfunction.

papers.title: Computational design of optimized and preferentially paired human TCR constant regions for improved T cell function.
papers.summary: Using computational protein design algorithms, the authors engineered human TCR constant regions for stability and preferential pairing. The resulting SeTC variant showed enhanced surface expression, functional avidity, reduced chain mispairing, increased cytokine secretion and cytotoxicity, and potent tumor control in xenografts; benefits were reproduced across six different TCRs, supporting broad applicability.

papers.title: Transmembrane delivery of antimicrobial peptides by engineered eCIS into macrophages for intracellular mycobacteria elimination.
papers.summary: An engineered Photorhabdus virulence cassette (eCIS) delivers mycobacteriophage-derived antimicrobial peptides into CD11b-targeted alveolar macrophages, inhibiting intracellular Mycobacterium smegmatis, M. bovis, M. tuberculosis, and an isoniazid-resistant strain. Pulmonary mycobacterial load in infected mice fell more than tenfold with reduced inflammation, demonstrating intracellular biomacromolecule delivery against drug-resistant mycobacteria.

papers.title: Ultrasound-enhanced exosome secretion and antibody-free SERS profiling for Alzheimer's disease via iPSC-derived cortical organoids.
papers.summary: Ultrasound stimulation increased exosome secretion from iPSC-derived cortical organoids, and label-free surface-enhanced Raman scattering profiling of intact exosomes distinguished apolipoprotein E genotype-dependent fingerprints. Transcriptomics confirmed upregulated exosome-related genes linked to Alzheimer's pathology, providing an ultrasound-enhanced, label-free precision diagnostic framework for genotype-specific Alzheimer's disease signatures.

papers.title: Spatial organization of AQP4 water channel expression in the human brain.
papers.summary: AQP4 water-channel expression is highly spatially organized in the human brain, peaking in subcortical, ventral, and periventricular territories near CSF reservoirs. AQP4-enriched regions show lower perfusion, lie near small-vessel disease areas, colocalize with tau and TDP-43 atrophy patterns, and match glioma frequency, linking glymphatic anatomy to disease vulnerability.

papers.title: Persistent TOP1 cleavage complexes in drug-tolerant cells drive adaptive resistance to EGFR-targeted therapies in lung cancer.
papers.summary: EGFR inhibition in EGFR-mutated lung cancer downregulates TDP1, the TOP1 cleavage-complex repair enzyme. In drug-tolerant cells, ROS promote TOP1cc trapping while impaired repair drives mutation accumulation and reproliferation. About 25% of EGFR-mutant tumors lack TDP1, and adding sublethal topotecan to EGFR inhibition abolished reproliferation, revealing a targetable resistance mechanism.

papers.title: The effect of microgravity and flows on the organization and dynamics of the human genome.
papers.summary: Simulated microgravity changes nuclear size and shape and visibly affects nucleolar liquid phases, but genome organization and dynamics remain largely preserved; fluid flows cause DNA damage while microgravity does not. The human genome shows robust mechanical homeostasis, providing biophysical insight into gravity's role in nuclear organization and function.

papers.title: An ASXL3-thyroid hormone axis in parvalbumin interneurons controls autism-like behaviors.
papers.summary: ASXL3 haploinsufficiency derepresses the thyroid hormone-inactivating enzyme DIO3 via altered H2A monoubiquitination, depleting brain thyroid hormone, expanding parvalbumin interneurons, and causing autism-like behaviors. Neonatal thyroid hormone supplementation restored interneuron numbers and behavior within a critical early window, and an intein-based AAV reconstituting full-length ASXL3 normalized architecture in mice and non-human primates.

papers.title: High-fidelity genotyping and therapeutic oligonucleotides analysis by liquid-phase ion trap coupled with mass spectrometry.
papers.summary: A liquid-phase ion trap uses strong electric fields to dissociate metal contaminants and enrich nucleic acid ions in solution, improving mass accuracy up to 48-fold and signal intensity 100-fold for intact DNA. Demonstrations include high-resolution genotyping, rapid influenza subtyping from raw PCR products, and impurity detection in therapeutic oligonucleotides.

papers.title: Ancient Nuclear Genome Duplication Events in Vertebrates Facilitated the Functional Diversification of Ohnologous Cytochrome c: Insights from Buergeria Frogs.
papers.summary: Vertebrate cytochrome c ohnologs arose through ancient whole-genome duplication, diverging into somatic- and testis-type paralogs conserved for ~450-540 million years. Testis-type proteins carry Tyr46 facing the heme, conferring higher hydrogen peroxide resistance than somatic Phe46; mutating Tyr46 to Phe reduced resistance, linking genome duplication to tissue-specific mitochondrial functional diversification.

papers.title: p63 and p73 drive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma through convergent transcriptional control of EGFR signaling.
papers.summary: p63 and p73 are upregulated and cooperatively required in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. They form heteromeric complexes, co-occupy distal enhancers, sustain cell-cycle progression, restrain apoptotic programs, and co-regulate EGFR ligands - with amphiregulin as a key mitogenic mediator whose depletion impairs tumor formation, linking enhancer co-occupancy to squamous tumor maintenance.

papers.title: DDX39A unwinds viral RNA G-quadruplexes to limit α-Synuclein amyloidogenesis.
papers.summary: The DEAD-box helicase DDX39A interacts with alpha-synuclein via RNA G-quadruplexes and unwinds them, decelerating alpha-synuclein amyloidogenesis. Viral infections elevate cytoplasmic G-quadruplexes, and viral sequences from H1N1 and SARS-CoV-2 accelerate aggregation, while DDX39A overexpression rescues infected primary neurons - proposing a mechanism for the viral etiology of Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: LiP-MS reveals a feedback loop of tomato UDP-glucosyltransferases managing bioactive jasmonate homeostasis.
papers.summary: Limited proteolysis-mass spectrometry identified jasmonic acid-binding proteins in tomato, including UDP-glycosyltransferases. Two UGTs glucosylate jasmonic acid into jasmonoyl-glucosyl esters, characterized by omics, biochemical, enzymatic, and structural analyses, uncovering a missing catabolic step that helps regulate bioactive jasmonate homeostasis in plants.

papers.title: Transcriptional and epigenomic analysis of insulin sensitivity in human adipocytes.
papers.summary: Transcriptional and epigenomic profiling of adipocytes from insulin-sensitive versus insulin-resistant subjects identified differential regulatory elements near IRS1. CRISPRi repression pinpointed two enhancer regions that regulate IRS1 expression in a cell-state-dependent manner, and specific transcription factors acting through these sites were identified, defining molecular events underlying human insulin sensitivity.

papers.title: Components of an ESCRT-independent nuclear envelope assembly pathway.
papers.summary: In fission yeast, Alx1 functions in a Cmp7- and ESCRT-independent nuclear envelope assembly pathway via positive regulation of the conserved protein Vid27. Vid27 localizes to postmitotic envelope sealing sites, is essential, and interacts with Alx1; mutations disrupting the predicted interface abolish Alx1's enhancement, defining components of a new envelope sealing pathway.

papers.title: MicroRNA circuits and regulatory networks: emerging therapeutic paradigm.
papers.summary: This review describes miRNA-transcription factor regulatory circuits - feedback and feedforward loops enabling precise gene-expression control - and how mathematical modeling and machine learning reveal their global structure in cell fate selection, stress adaptation, and disease. Insights open prospects for biomarker discovery and therapeutic approaches, particularly in cancer and immunotherapy.

papers.title: Dynamic flow-driven in vitro skin model reveals mechanosensitive remodeling pathways.
papers.summary: A 3D keratinocyte-fibroblast co-culture in collagen subjected to unidirectional fluid flow showed enhanced keratinocyte stratification (CK14, involucrin), increased proliferation, elevated fibroblast density, and selective ERK and p38 MAPK activation. The flow-driven model recapitulates key responses to mechanical stress, providing a platform for studying mechanosensitive skin remodeling pathways.

papers.title: O-GlcNAcylation in Macrophage Functions.
papers.summary: This review summarizes how O-GlcNAcylation, the reversible modification catalyzed by OGT and OGA, integrates glucose flux through the hexosamine pathway with macrophage biology - influencing pattern-recognition receptor expression and localization, endosome maturation, phagocytosis, reactive oxygen species production, and pro- versus anti-inflammatory polarization, all tightly coupled to metabolic state.

papers.title: Explaining the unexplained admixture mapping signals via rare variants: the HCHS/SOL.
papers.summary: Using whole-genome sequencing plus metabolomics in the Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos, rare variant sets explained only a small fraction of previously unexplained admixture mapping signals, whereas common variants from larger genomic regions explained most. The work provides a strategy for fine-mapping and causal variant identification in admixed populations.

papers.title: The evolution of male courtship discrimination is driven by sympatry and age-dependent pheromones between Drosophila athabasca species complex and its congeners.
papers.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
papers.summary: Across ten Drosophila affinis subgroup species pairs, male courtship discrimination increased with sympatry when postzygotic isolation was present. Age-dependent cuticular hydrocarbons - 11(Z)-tricosene, 10,14-pentacosadiene, and 2-methylhexacosane - diverge with sexual maturity and carry species-specific repellent or aphrodisiac activity, enabling males to avoid maladaptive hybridization in sympatry.

papers.title: Phylogenetic patterns of tolerance to herbivory and underlying suite of traits: phylogenetic signal and trade-offs.
papers.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
papers.summary: A common-garden defoliation experiment across Datura with phylogenetic comparative analysis found no overall phylogenetic signal in tolerance to herbivory, signal only in some underlying traits (specific leaf area, chlorophyll), and no tolerance-resistance trade-off. A fitness cost of tolerance appears as reduced performance without damage, suggesting complementary defenses shaped by resource allocation.

papers.title: Organelle scaling over a 100-fold cell size range.
papers.summary: In the polymorphic fungus Aureobasidium pullulans, whose proliferating cells span roughly a 100-fold volume range, mitochondrial and ER content scale proportionally with cell volume while vacuoles and peroxisomes do not. This shows organelle composition is affected by cell volume when size variation is large, unlike within typical proliferating populations.

papers.title: Organelle partitioning in the multi-budding yeast Aureobasidium pullulans.
papers.summary: First characterization of organelle inheritance in a fungus that multi-buds, producing up to 20 daughters per cycle: mitochondria and ER are delivered evenly to all growing buds, while vacuoles and peroxisomes are inherited more variably. The findings extend organelle partitioning principles beyond cells that divide in half.

papers.title: The heterodimeric amino acid transporters (HAT) of the SLC7/SLC3 family: A structure-function relationships and relevance to human pathology.
papers.summary: This review updates structure-function relationships of SLC7/SLC3 heterodimeric amino acid transporters (LAT1, y+LAT2, Asc1, xCT, and others), noting that SLC3 subunits mainly assist trafficking of the transport subunits rather than transport themselves, and discusses how altered transporter expression, function, or localization underlies human disease.

papers.title: Smaller is better: nanobodies meet NMR.
papers.summary: This review covers nanobody-assisted NMR spectroscopy: single-domain camelid antibodies act as chaperones that stabilize flexible regions, reduce conformational heterogeneity, and improve spectral quality for membrane proteins, large complexes, and intrinsically disordered proteins, enabling selective labeling and probing of dynamic interactions under near-physiological conditions, with emphasis on drug discovery applications.

papers.title: Atrial natriuretic peptide may inhibit motion sickness through reducing aldosterone-induced increase in endolymph volume of the inner ear.
papers.summary: Rotatory stimulation raised plasma aldosterone, and aldosterone injection caused motion sickness-like responses in rodents that atrial natriuretic peptide blocked. ANP alleviated aldosterone-induced endolymph expansion, reduced inner-ear mineralocorticoid receptor expression and downstream ion transporters (ENaC, Na+-K+-ATPase), suggesting ANP inhibits motion sickness by counteracting aldosterone-driven endolymph volume increases.

papers.title: Exploring the cytotoxic potential of Artemisia herba-alba crude extract and key phytoconstituents using in vitro assays and molecular docking insights.
papers.summary: Aqueous Artemisia herba-alba extract showed selective in vitro cytotoxicity, with lower IC50 values against breast (MDA-MB-231) and colon (HCT-116) cancer cells (80-100 ug/mL) than against normal HUVECs or pancreatic PANC-1 cells. UHPLC-MS/MS identified artemisinin, isofraxidin, and liquiritigenin, and docking favored TP53-isofraxidin and TP53-liquiritigenin complexes, supporting phenolic-mediated anticancer potential.

papers.title: Eastern African expressions of suffering: A new Cultural Scripts of Trauma Inventory.
papers.summary: A qualitative study (115 participants) and quantitative validation (1,208 participants) across Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania, and Kenya produced a 15-item Cultural Scripts of Trauma Inventory spanning cognitive, body-related, frame-of-mind, meaning-disruption, and family-stress factors, with strong reliability, validity, and measurement invariance - advancing culturally informed trauma assessment beyond PTSD criteria.

papers.title: Deep learning-based spatial immunoprofiling of multiplex immunofluorescence images distinguishes tuberculosis disease states in diversity outbred mice.
papers.summary: Deep learning-based segmentation of multiplex immunofluorescence images from M. tuberculosis-infected diversity outbred mice distinguishes disease states by granuloma spatial features. Asymptomatic infection showed higher CD4/CD8 T cell densities, closer B cell proximity to bronchiolar epithelium, and increased T cell-macrophage proximity; an LLM independently decoded cellular patterns, establishing an automated granuloma-analysis pipeline.

papers.title: Alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase (NAGLU) inactivation causes morphological damage to the ultrastructural appearance of epididymal mononuclear phagocytes (eMPs) and epithelial cells of the epididymis in adult mice.
papers.summary: In Naglu-/- mice (Sanfilippo syndrome type B), pale lysosomes massively accumulate in epididymal principal cells and epididymal mononuclear phagocytes, damaging ER, Golgi, mitochondria, and nuclei. Phagocytes contained 'zebra bodies' reactive for a mitochondrial marker, suggesting engulfment of degenerating principal cells - linking NAGLU loss to a disrupted epididymal environment for sperm maturation.

papers.title: Genome-wide assessment of genetic diversity and population structure of Capsicum in Southwestern Colombia using DArTseq markers.
papers.summary: Genotyping 69 Capsicum accessions across seven species from southwestern Colombia with 3,681 DArT-SNP markers revealed low observed heterozygosity, high inbreeding coefficients, and retained genetic variability. Clear differentiation separated Andean from domesticated species, and markers distinguished wild from domesticated C. annuum and C. frutescens, informing conservation and breeding programs.

papers.title: Identification and mechanistic investigation of novel biomarkers for diabetic retinopathy through hypoxia- and cuproptosis-associated gene analysis.
papers.summary: Intersecting diabetic retinopathy datasets with hypoxia- and cuproptosis-related genes, machine learning identified MED19 and CA11 as consistently downlinked biomarkers with AUC above 0.70 in both datasets. Functional enrichment linked MED19 to proteasome/spliceosome and CA11 to autophagy regulation, with differential immune cell infiltration and candidate therapeutic compounds identified.

papers.title: Modulation of angiogenic transcription factor ERG via miR-6756 and miR-3190.
papers.summary: miR-6756 and miR-3190 each have three predicted binding sites on ERG mRNA. Overexpression in primary endothelial cells significantly reduced ERG mRNA and protein, its transcriptional activity, endothelial cell migration, and angiogenic targets including VE-cadherin, indicating both microRNAs regulate the angiogenic transcription factor ERG and downstream angiogenesis signaling.

papers.title: BCAM-AKT2 fusion protein promotes unfolded protein response driven oncogenic signaling in SKOV3 epithelial ovarian cancer cell line.
papers.summary: The BCAM-AKT2 fusion protein promotes proliferation in SKOV3 epithelial ovarian cancer cells. RNA-seq shows the fusion activates unfolded protein response signaling while inhibiting interferon alpha/beta signaling, pyroptosis, and viral response pathways, suggesting BCAM-AKT2 modulates UPR-linked oncogenic networks and represents a promising therapeutic target in ovarian cancer.

papers.title: Early electrophysiological responses reflect precision-weighted prediction errors to face features.
papers.summary: Modeling EEG responses with a hierarchical Gaussian filter, facial feature processing reflected precision-weighted prediction errors, with peak effects around 140 ms post-stimulus. The findings show prediction errors for complex social stimuli are computed early during face processing, supporting rapid updating of predictive models during social interaction.

papers.title: Two opposite effects of desmoglein 3 on the growth of oral squamous cell carcinoma between anchorage -dependent and -independent conditions.
papers.summary: Desmoglein 3 shows opposite effects in oral squamous cell carcinoma depending on anchorage: it suppresses proliferation in anchorage-dependent conditions, whereas under anchorage-independent conditions it is upregulated and supports structural organization of multicellular aggregates without affecting proliferation. This context-dependent behavior may explain paradoxical DSG3 effects and facilitate tumor adaptation to metastatic environments.

papers.title: Comparative evolutionary pharmacogenomics of human prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase paralogs identifies population-structured coding variation and protein-contextual candidates in N-terminal leader-sequence and catalytic-channel regions.
papers.summary: Integrating population differentiation, transcript consequence annotation, splice predictions, and protein structural context for PTGS1/PTGS2 (NSAID targets), the study prioritized candidates including PTGS1 leader-sequence variants and PTGS2 Val511Ala near the rofecoxib-contact network. Docking showed no systematic variant effects, establishing a calibrated framework for experimentally testable pharmacogenomic candidates.

papers.title: Comparative transcriptomics reveals stage-specific regulatory pathways of ear thickening in Auricularia polytricha.
papers.summary: Comparative transcriptomics of a thick-ear Auricularia polytricha mutant across three developmental stages revealed stage-specific pathways: primordium-stage genes enriched in energy and substance synthesis, young-ear genes in cell proliferation and structure formation, and mature-stage genes in protein synthesis and cellular homeostasis - supporting molecular marker-assisted breeding for ear thickness.

papers.title: Effects of platelet-rich fibrin on the biological properties of rabbit adipose-derived stem cells in vitro.
papers.summary: Platelet-rich fibrin formed three-dimensional fibrin networks and significantly enhanced rabbit adipose-derived stem cell proliferation from day 3 onward and migration in scratch assays, with direct co-culture within the 3D scaffold outperforming indirect culture. The PRF/ADSC composite showed favorable cytocompatibility, warranting in vivo testing in urethral defect models.

papers.title: Expression of long non‑coding RNAs DIAPH3‑AS1, HMMR‑AS1, and SPATA3‑AS1 in patients with colorectal cancer: association with chemotherapy response and clinicopathological features.
papers.summary: The antisense lncRNAs DIAPH3-AS1, HMMR-AS1, and SPATA3-AS1 are all upregulated in colorectal cancer versus healthy mucosa. Only HMMR-AS1 fell after capecitabine-based chemotherapy and tracked differentiation grade; none associated with stage, metastasis, or treatment response, and diagnostic AUCs were modest, indicating transcript-specific roles in colorectal cancer biology.

papers.title: Dysregulation of circadian clock gene BMAL1 and cell cycle regulator WEE1 in pediatric AML.
papers.summary: In 40 pediatric acute myeloid leukemia bone marrow samples, the circadian clock gene BMAL1 (~0.18-fold) and cell cycle regulator WEE1 (~0.31-fold) were significantly downregulated versus controls. BMAL1 inversely correlated with white blood cell count and blast percentage, suggesting disrupted circadian and cell-cycle pathways in pediatric AML pathogenesis.

papers.title: Stress granules and RNA-binding proteins in cellular senescence: a modular perspective on stress adaptation and inflammation.
papers.summary: This review examines how stress granules and RNA-binding proteins (G3BP1/2, TIA1/TIAR, TDP-43, and others) intersect with cellular senescence, including SASP, cGAS-STING, NF-kB, and interferon signaling. A stage-resolved modular framework positions stress granules as context-dependent inflammatory components rather than universal inducers of senescence onset.

papers.title: 2,8-Dihydroxyquinoline ameliorates oligoasthenozoospermia by inhibiting MAPK14-mediated spermatogonial ferroptosis.
papers.summary: 2,8-Dihydroxyquinoline, identified as a key metabolite of XHBG, binds MAPK14 (confirmed by DARTS), downregulates it, and restores sperm parameters and testicular architecture in mice with drug-induced oligoasthenozoospermia. Protection proceeds through ferroptosis suppression - reduced iron, ROS, and lipid peroxidation with restored SLC7A11/GPX4 - abolished by MAPK14 overexpression.

papers.title: Replication protein A prevents unregulated priming and Rad51 loading on single-stranded DNA in nuclear extracts of Xenopus eggs.
papers.summary: In Xenopus egg extracts, excess single-stranded DNA induces spontaneous primer synthesis normally suppressed by replication protein A. RPA stoichiometrically binds ssDNA and recruits ATR checkpoint factors, pol alpha-primase, and RFWD3; depletion instead recruits Rad51, paralogs, and the fork-breaking helicase FBH1, showing RPA guards against unscheduled DNA synthesis and recombination.

papers.title: Juanbi Qianggu Formula Alleviates Rheumatoid Arthritis by Suppressing the TNF-α/NF-κB Signaling Pathway.
papers.summary: Juanbi Qianggu Formula ameliorated collagen-induced arthritis in mice with efficacy comparable to methotrexate, reducing TNF-alpha. In macrophages its serum suppressed NF-kB p65 nuclear translocation and, per transcriptomics with rescue assays, directly suppressed TNFAIP2 via the primary NF-kB axis, disrupting an NF-kB/TNFAIP2/ROS inflammatory cascade underlying rheumatoid arthritis.

papers.title: Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cells Improve PINK1/PARKIN-Mediated Mitophagy Inhibition in Preeclampsia.
papers.summary: In LPS-induced preeclampsia cell models and L-NAME rats, umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells restored PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy that was inhibited in preeclampsia, increasing ATP and mitochondrial membrane potential. Transplantation alleviated hypertension, proteinuria, and angiogenic imbalance and improved pregnancy outcomes, supporting UC-MSCs as a candidate preeclampsia therapy.

papers.title: Cell-Type-Dependent Responses to Oleuropein in MDA-MB-231 Breast Cancer Cells and HUVECs.
papers.summary: Oleuropein reduced MDA-MB-231 triple-negative breast cancer cell viability, clonogenicity, and wound closure in a time-dependent manner, with increased BAX/CDKN1B and decreased BCL2, while HUVECs responded oppositely. These cell-type-dependent effects - antiproliferative in cancer cells, pro-survival in endothelial cells - support further oleuropein investigation in breast cancer models.

papers.title: EphA2 Silencing Attenuates IL-1β-Induced Chondrocyte Ferroptosis and Extracellular Matrix Degradation In Vitro.
papers.summary: In IL-1beta-stimulated rat chondrocytes modeling osteoarthritis, EphA2 silencing restored collagen II and aggrecan, reduced ADAMTS-5/MMP-13, decreased apoptosis, and attenuated ferroptosis - lowering iron and lipid peroxidation while restoring GSH and GPX4/SLC7A11 and reducing ACSL4 - identifying EphA2 as a contributor to chondrocyte ferroptosis in osteoarthritis.

papers.title: Crosstalk Between Nrf2 and Metabolic Pathways: Redox Regulation, Glutaminolysis, and Cellular Proliferation.
papers.summary: This narrative review argues Nrf2 controls both antioxidant defense and metabolism - pentose phosphate pathway, glutamine catabolism, NADPH regeneration, purine synthesis - so its dual role in tumors reflects substrate supply rather than proliferative instruction. Isotope-tracing examples span pulmonary fibrosis, the diabetic heart, and tumor progression, guiding tissue-matched Nrf2-directed therapies.

papers.title: Green Synthesis, Physicochemical Characterization, and In Vitro Biological Evaluation of Moringa concanensis-Mediated Zinc Oxide Nanoparticles with Keratinocyte Wound-Closure Activity.
papers.summary: Zinc oxide nanoparticles green-synthesized with Moringa concanensis leaf extract (~35 nm crystalline wurtzite phase) showed antioxidant and antidiabetic enzyme-inhibitory activity, low HaCaT keratinocyte cytotoxicity, and improved in vitro scratch wound closure. Without nanoparticle controls the contribution of ZnO versus surface phytochemicals cannot be separated, and mechanistic and in vivo studies are needed.

papers.title: Ergothioneine Modulates Inflammatory Signaling in LPS-Stimulated RAW 264.7 Macrophages.
papers.summary: A validated HPLC-DAD method quantified ergothioneine in Hericium erinaceus; network pharmacology flagged HSP90AA1 as a shared inflammatory bowel disease target with stable docking. In LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages, ergothioneine reduced iNOS and COX-2 expression and modulated PPAR-gamma, supporting anti-inflammatory potential requiring disease-model validation.

papers.title: Integrating evolutionary signals and predicted protein structure reveals localized molecular divergence in Cereus lineages.
papers.summary: Integrating branch-site positive-selection candidates with predicted protein structures in the Cereus fernambucensis-insularis clade showed divergence concentrated in flexible loops and surface-exposed regions near predicted cavities, with heterogeneous stability effects and conserved global folds - demonstrating structure-informed evolutionary inference for adaptive genes in non-model organisms.

papers.title: Molecular phylogenetics, distribution and evolution of the TPP riboswitch.
papers.summary: Phylogenetic and covariation analyses trace TPP riboswitch evolution: an early prokaryotic origin as a 5' UTR regulator, archaeal retention of the compact ancestral scaffold, strongest covariation in bacteria, 3' UTR repositioning in the green lineage predating land plants, and fungal alternative configurations acquired by horizontal transfer from early green lineages.
